newsitem.title: UK: UniChem says Lloyds offer not final.
newsitem.headline: UniChem says Lloyds offer not final.

text.p: UniChem finance director Geoff Cooper said the company's offer for UK pharmacy and drug wholesaler Lloyds Chemists was not final.
"It's not a final offer, but we think this is the best offer to people right now," said Cooper in an interview.
Earlier the company renewed its takeover bid for Lloyds, offering 505.4 pence for each Lloyds share, valuing the company at 657.6 million pounds ($1.03 billion).
That is one percent higher than the 649.9 million-pound cash bid offered in February by German based Gehe -- Europe's largest drug distributor.
Cooper also reiterated comments made by UniChem's chief executive Jeffery Harris. "If they want to buy the business then why don't they come out and bid," Cooper said.
Earlier Gehe said it is evaluating its position after UniChem renewed its bid for Lloyds Chemists, adding that it was still interested in acquiring Lloyds.
Gehe also questioned UniChem's claim that its acquisition of Lloyds would enhance earnings after the first 12 months.
In a statement to the London stock exchange Gehe also asked if UniChem had the experience to integrate Lloyds Chemists effectively. -- Tim Farrand, London Newsroom +44 171 542 6437
